name: Isack Lugata
hero: Hey! I'm Isack Lugata. I build websites, mobile apps, and AI-powered products that work for real people.
intro: Full-stack & mobile developer in Dar es Salaam. Co-founder of Ecofy Africa. Open to freelance projects.
aboutHero: I take ideas apart, figure out how the pieces fit, and build software that works for people.
about: I'm Isack Lugata, a full-stack and mobile developer based in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania. I work across frontend interfaces, backend services, mobile applications, and applied AI, taking an idea from the screen to the systems behind it.

I co-founded Ecofy Africa, where I work on both the frontend and backend alongside the AI and product direction. My other work spans marketplaces, legal technology, property platforms, and internal business systems.

I am the former chairperson of the 3D Solutions & Robotics Lab at UDSM CoICT. My contribution there included backend development, and our team worked on projects such as Nena AI and TanStack Tanzania. That experience brought software, research, and collaboration into the same room.

Different projects need different contributions. At GloboExpats, mine is mainly frontend; at Osher Market and TanStack, it is backend. I also develop mobile apps and help connect interfaces, APIs, data, and AI into a working product. Outside work: chess, basketball, video editing, and experiments driven by curiosity.

services.title: Frontend & web apps
services.description: Responsive websites, product interfaces, and web applications. Clear user journeys, thoughtful interaction, and frontend work connected to real APIs.

services.title: Mobile apps
services.description: Mobile applications built around clear interfaces, reliable APIs, and practical everyday workflows, from the first screen to the services behind it.

services.title: Backend & integrations
services.description: Python APIs, authentication, databases, payments, messaging, and internal management systems. Built with deployment and maintenance in mind.

services.title: Applied AI
services.description: AI assistants, retrieval over your documents, document processing, and language-model integrations for useful English and Swahili experiences.

projects.name: Ecofy Africa
projects.summary: Ecofy Africa brings farm planning, activity records, and agricultural guidance into one product for Tanzanian farmers. I am a co-founder, CEO and AI Lead, and work on both the frontend and backend.
story: Ecofy helps farmers plan their season, record work, monitor costs, and understand the next useful action on their farm.
My contribution spans the frontend and backend, alongside AI services and technical product direction. I work with a team across the product.
The public experience is designed around Swahili-speaking users, with farm information, growing-season tasks, weather, and market information presented together.
The engineering work connects product interfaces, APIs, data, and AI assistance. I care about how those parts work together for the person using them.
The live website is at ecofy.co.tz, with a linked farm application. The preview shown here is captured from the public site.
projects.role: Frontend & backend · Co-founder, CEO & AI Lead
projects.status: Public website and linked farm application

projects.name: Wakili Msomi
projects.summary: Wakili Msomi is an AI-powered legal-information application for the Tanzanian context. I worked on both its frontend and backend, connecting the user-facing experience with the services behind it.
story: The application brings legal-information assistance and document workflows into a digital interface for Tanzanian users.
My contribution covered both frontend and backend development, rather than only the AI layer. The interface and its underlying services are part of the same product experience.
The work builds on my practical-training experience at Bluefin Solutions in collaboration with Sheria Kiganjani, with English and Swahili users in mind.
The linked public application currently presents sign-in and registration. The screenshot shows that public entry point, without exposing private conversations or documents.

projects.name: GloboExpats
projects.summary: GloboExpats is a marketplace for the expat community in Tanzania. My work is mainly on the frontend: the interfaces people use to browse, discover, buy, and sell.
story: The public marketplace brings goods, services, homes, vehicles, and community requests into a browsing experience centered on Dar es Salaam.
My contribution is mainly frontend development, working on the interfaces people use to explore the marketplace and move between product workflows.
The interface brings together category browsing, listings, seller information, and the paths into buying and selling.
For a marketplace, frontend work is about helping people understand what is available and move naturally from browsing into the next step.
The screenshot is from the live public marketplace. The link opens GloboExpats directly.

projects.name: Habitek
projects.summary: Habitek combines property discovery with property and hospitality management in Tanzania. I worked on both the frontend and backend of the platform.
story: The public experience helps people explore places to live or work, while the management side brings properties, units, tenants, and everyday operations together.
My contribution covers frontend and backend development: the interfaces and the application services that support them.
The linked website and captured preview show the public property-discovery experience. Internal management data and account screens are not included.

projects.name: Osher Market
projects.summary: Osher Market is a commerce and business platform. My contribution is backend development: the application services behind the marketplace experience.
story: The public storefront organizes products into categories and gives buyers and sellers an entry point into the platform.
My contribution is backend development. The public storefront preview shows the product that those application services support.
This work sits behind the interface, in the services and application logic that support a commerce product.
The live link opens Osher Market. Detailed internal service design can be discussed in a project enquiry without publishing private operational information.

projects.name: Falco management backend
projects.summary: Falco management backend supports internal management workflows. I contributed backend development for the company, separately from its public marketing website.
story: This project centers on an internal business-management system, rather than a public-facing website.
My contribution is backend development for management workflows and the application logic behind them.
The visual is a conceptual backend sketch, not a screenshot of Falco's internal system. It contains no real accounts, records, or operational data.
The external link is Falco's public company website for context. It should not be read as a claim that I built that website or its frontend.

projects.name: TanStack Tanzania
projects.summary: TanStack Tanzania connects tech students with opportunities, learning resources, and career support. I worked on its backend as part of our lab's project work.
story: The platform brings opportunities, resources, a company directory, and CV support into one place for Tanzanian tech students.
My contribution is backend development for the platform. The public preview gives context to the student-facing product.
TanStack is one of the projects associated with our work at the 3D Solutions & Robotics Lab, alongside Nena AI.
The live website is available at tanstack.co.tz. The screenshot shows its public interface; individual student records and private account information are not shown.
